investigation.title: Remote Agent Provisioning: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-31T15:26–15:27Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at POST /api/agents before any agent identity is returned, zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, causing a complete contract violation for the remote-agent-create eval.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed upstream that the production-api proxies agent-creation requests to at /v1/agents — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)" for every remote-agents check. Because the gateway failure happens before the agent is provisioned, no VM is allocated and no evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are ever written, causing the eval to fail both the contract-evidence check and all assertions. This is an eval-observed infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: Primary: The swarm gateway ELB (us-east-2) was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run, causing the production-api to receive a connection error and surface it as a 502.
Secondary: A network routing or security-group change between the production-api and the swarm gateway ELB blocked outbound requests to /v1/agents, producing the 'error sending request' message.
Tertiary: The swarm gateway service itself (the process behind the ELB) crashed or was being redeployed, leaving the ELB with zero healthy instances and returning 502 to all callers.

Lower probability: A transient DNS resolution failure for the ELB hostname caused the connection attempt to fail; this would produce the same 'error sending request' message but would likely be intermittent rather than affecting all three sequential checks.

investigation.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI Credit Balance Exhausted on /api/generate/image/stream
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to return a hard error (code: credit_balance_exhausted). The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame, so both contract assertions — frameTypes contains "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equals true — were violated. This is an eval infrastructure / API credential failure, not a confirmed user-facing product outage.
investigation.rootCause: The OpenAI organization account whose API key is used by the eval runner at /api/generate/image/stream has exhausted its credit balance. The OpenAI API rejected the image generation request with error type "insufficient_quota" and code "credit_balance_exhausted" before any image could be produced. As a result, the SSE stream emitted a generation_error frame and closed without ever emitting a generation_completed frame or an image artifact URL, causing both required contract assertions to fail.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Provisioning: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-31T15:26–15:27Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at POST /api/agents before any agent identity is returned, zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, causing a complete contract violation for the remote-agent-create eval.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed upstream that the production-api proxies agent-creation requests to at /v1/agents — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)" for every remote-agents check. Because the gateway failure happens before the agent is provisioned, no VM is allocated and no evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are ever written, causing the eval to fail both the contract-evidence check and all assertions. This is an eval-observed infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-runtime, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) failed at 2026-08-31T15:26–15:27Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api's POST /api/agents endpoint could not reach the swarm ELB at http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents during agent provisioning. Because agent creation is the first step in every remote-agents eval flow, the swarm gateway being unreachable caused all downstream evidence collection to be skipped entirely, leaving zero required evidence fields populated.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check calls POST /api/agents as its first step (evidenced by the runner calling createAgent at run-status-probes.mjs:1918), and all three checks received the same "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning" 502 response within a ~22-second window. This is an eval-observed infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency of the remote-agents provisioning path; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.
